label: Lithium fire risk
summary: Damaged, swollen, overcharged or shorted lithium cells can heat up by themselves, vent toxic and flammable gas, and burn violently. One cell can set off the next. Lots of water cools a burning pack but doesn't reliably stop it, and cells can reignite hours later.
signs: Swollen or puffy pouch cells, or a phone, laptop or tablet case lifting or bulging
A cell or pack hot to the touch when not in use or charging
Hissing, popping, a sweet chemical smell, or smoke
Dents, punctures, crushed corners, leaks or rust
Scorch marks, melted plastic or torn cell wrapping
Cells that have sat flat for a long time, below about 2 V
do: Move a damaged cell or device outdoors onto bare earth, sand or concrete, away from anything that burns; if it's hissing, smoking or too hot to hold, use a shovel or metal tongs, or leave it and get out
Keep damaged cells in a metal box of dry sand with a loose lid, away from where people sleep
Charge on a non-flammable surface where you can watch it, and stop if it gets hot
Keep a bucket of sand or dirt and a shovel where you charge

If a cell or pack catches fire: get everyone out and keep clear of the smoke; only if it's small and you can do it safely, drown it with lots of water or shovel it outdoors and cover it with sand or dirt, then leave it there for a day
dont: Don't puncture, crush, bend or cut cells
Don't charge swollen, dented or hot cells, or cells that have sat below about 2 V
Don't charge lithium cells below freezing (0 °C)
Don't carry loose cells in a pocket with keys or coins
Don't seal damaged cells in an airtight container: gas pressure builds up
Don't leave anything charging overnight in your shelter
ppe: Work outdoors or right next to an open exit
A working smoke alarm where you charge and in the rooms where you sleep, tested regularly
firstAid: Smoke breathed in: get to fresh air; coughing, wheezing or breathlessness needs medical care, and can start up to a day later
Burns: cool under cool running water for 20 minutes and cover loosely
Electrolyte on skin or in eyes: rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes
